(i) The SPS beam-beam limit is determined by the beam-beam effect.

1) the beam-beam effect is the limiting factor for the beam lifetime in the SPS, 2) the beam-beams effect can be reduced by the use of a large horizontal crossing angle, 3) the beam-beem effect is reduced by the presence of a large vertical crossing angle, 4) a large vertical crossing-angle reduces the beam-beam limit on the beam lifetime, 5) a large horizontal crossing-angle reduces the effect of single-bunch instabilities,
the SPS beam-beam effect is strong, that it is the main limiting factor for the luminosity, and that its effects are not fully understood.

the SPS beam-beam interaction is a major problem in the operation of the collider.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beam-beam effect in SPS is a serious problem, which has to be taken into account in all aspects of the operation of the machine and the design of the experiments.
